body: I added the test case to [this branch](https://github.com/tbcs/netty/tree/issue_4906) for convenient assessment.

@tbcs - I think there may be an issue, but not where you expect. The `// FAIL` behavior you indicate is actually expected behavior. What you are doing is saying starting from the `firstContext()`'s perspective fire an event. This will basically pass the event to the next context in the pipeline. If you want to ensure all handlers in the pipeline get the event use `pipeline().fireChannelRegistered()`. I think the issue is that the all the handlers in `channelRegisteredShouldFireOnAddLastHandler` see the event, which is an issue in `EmbeddedChannel`.
@tbcs - Do I have permission to use / modify your unit test in a PR?

@Scottmitch - Thanks for looking into this.  The issue could be on my side, maybe I just misunderstood the API.

> I think the issue is that the all the handlers in `channelRegisteredShouldFireOnAddLastHandler` see the event, which is an issue in `EmbeddedChannel`.

Originally I encountered the problem in a project building on [RxNetty](https://github.com/ReactiveX/RxNetty), using epoll channels.  In the tests I made an attempt to isolate the issue, that's why I used `EmbeddedChannel`.  The source of my troubles could be the way `channelRegistered` gets propagated in RxNetty, so this might be a downstream issue.  I'll investigate further on the RxNetty side.

> Do I have permission to use / modify your unit test in a PR?

Sure!

issue.title: EmbeddedChannel Pipeline LastInboundHandler not always last

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body:
Motivation:
EmbeddedChannel was designed with the assumption that it can insert a handler in the pipeline at construction time and that handler will always be the last handler in the pipeline. This assumption does not hold true if the user modifies the pipeline with a addLast or similar type method. If the user does this the behavior of the pipeline for EmbeddedChannel will not mimic a real channel's behavior which will make testing scenarios less representative of real scenarios.

Modifications:
- Modify DefaultChannelPipeline so the tail handler can be configurable.
- Modify AbstractChannel to allow the tail of the DefaultChannelPipeline to be configured
- EmbeddedChannel no longer does an addLast but instead sets the tail element in the pipeline

Result:
EmbeddedChannel behaves more like a real channel implementation.
Fixes https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/4906

body:
I understand that there seems to be an issue with `EmbeddedChannel`'s handling of the pipeline.  However, I intended to report a different, unrelated issue.  I went back to check whether the behavior I experienced is specific to RxNetty and I can confirm that it is not.  After writing another test case I see now that the issue is specific to channel initialization, more specifically the way `ChannelInitializer`'s method `initChannel` is invoked.

@Scottmitch - I assume that you triaged this ticket according to the needs of the `EmbeddedChannel` issue, so I thought it's best to open a separate ticket for the `ChannelInitializer::initChannel` issue (it's filed under #4994).
